ref: step testflight-from-ci (TestFlight upload from CI); decision native-ships-via-testflight (iOS ships via TestFlight); item 65 (TestFlight from CI)
title: Where should CI read the Apple signing team id for TestFlight uploads?
holds: The first TestFlight upload from CI. Review of the lane goes on meanwhile.
context:
Goal: CI uploads TestFlight builds, as you picked on item 65 (option a).
Problem (risk): the upload tool ios-ship needs the Apple signing team id. On a GitHub runner it reads it only from env TEAM_ID, so every upload stops at "TEAM_ID is unset". Cloud sessions cannot set repo variables (GitHub API writes get 403).
Based on (read): ios-ship reads TEAM_ID from env first, then the team_id key of its config file (resolve TEAM_ID team_id).
Based on (ruling): decision native-ships-via-testflight says tools/ios-ship.json holds no ID; the team id lives off the repo.
Departs from: main — adds a repo variable TEAM_ID that .github/workflows/testflight.yml reads.

options.label: You add a repo variable TEAM_ID
options.how: Add the variable TEAM_ID on the repo's Actions variables page, with the same team id as on your Mac. The workflow reads it.
options.gain: No id in the public repo; the ruling stands.

options.label: Put team_id in tools/ios-ship.json
options.how: The lane writes the team id into the repo's ios-ship config file.
options.lose: The team id becomes public for good, against the ruling that the file holds no ID.

why: It keeps the id out of a public repo, and costs one press.
